description: Rebuild a disbanded sprint from a candidate of find_lost_sprints. Call it with apply=false first (the default): the answer says what would be done and changes nothing — 'sprint' (made: a new future sprint of that name; or the sprint itself while it is still open), 'issues' (the free ones, in the backlog now, that would go into it — 'count'), 'left' (in other sprints: they stay), 'refused', 'gone', 'hidden'. Then apply=true with expectIssues set to that 'count': another number by then refuses (count_mismatch). Here, the rebuild is ONE SET OF CHANGES — 'changeId', which rollback_sprint_change undoes in one call, the made sprint going back to the trash. On the linked Jira (an id starting with 'j') the sprint is made on the Jira project's first scrum board — or an open sprint of that name there is reused — and the issues are put into it through Jira Software's agile API on the project's token; that is written in Jira under the token owner's name, so it is applied only by a person signed in on the board's sprint trash, never by a token. A token configured into an agent or a script may preview; when issues would move it is refused (person_needed) — tell a person what the preview says. A sprint still in the trash is restored with restore_sprint instead (reason in_trash). Refusals have a 'reason': not_found, in_trash, nothing_free, expect_issues, count_mismatch, person_needed, forbidden, paused, scope (the Jira token lacks the scope named), refused, busy, unknown (the site did not answer after the request went — look there before trying again). Needs full write access to the project (member, admin or lead); a reporter, a commenter or a read-only member is refused with the reason, as is anybody while the project is paused or archived. Written in the project's journal under your name.

apply.description: false (the default) answers what would be done and changes nothing. true rebuilds — with expectIssues.

expectIssues.description: With apply=true: how many issues would go into the sprint, as the preview's 'count' said.

jiraProject.description: For a Jira candidate: the Jira project's key, as find_lost_sprints answered it.
